visual: A striking clump-forming perennial with large, deeply lobed, maple-like leaves in glowing copper-orange and burnt amber, dramatically marked with dark burgundy veins. Foliage darkens during summer and changes colour seasonally. Slender stems carry delicate sprays of small white flowers in spring and early summer.
water: Water regularly during establishment. Maintain moderately moist soil during active growth, particularly in warm weather and containers. Reduce watering during winter.
aspect: Partial shade or gentle morning sun. Tolerates fuller sun where soil moisture is reliable, but avoid scorching afternoon exposure.
soil: Fertile, humus-rich, moist but well-drained soil, preferably neutral.
soilWarning: Avoid prolonged waterlogging and excessively dry exposed sites. Keep the crown slightly above surrounding soil and mulch to prevent exposed rhizomes.
prune: Remove damaged or tired foliage in late winter or early spring. Deadhead spent flower stems. Divide established clumps every few years to maintain vigour.
toxicity: No significant toxicity commonly reported. Not intended for consumption.
compliance: Protected cultivar (PBR); check propagation rights before commercial multiplication.
hardinessNote: Fully hardy across the UK in suitable well-drained soil. Foliage may deteriorate during severe winters but growth normally resumes in spring.
resilience: Good cold tolerance and dependable shade performance. Sensitive to prolonged drought and root waterlogging; container specimens may attract vine weevil.
uses: Shaded borders, woodland planting, colourful ground cover, containers, pathway edging and underplanting shrubs.

visual: A compact woodland perennial with deeply lobed, glossy mid-green leaves marked by striking dark burgundy to chocolate-brown centres. In spring, upright, airy flower spikes display masses of tiny pale pink to blush-white, star-shaped flowers, creating a soft, frothy effect above the attractive foliage.
water: Keep soil consistently moist during the growing season, especially during establishment and prolonged dry spells. Reduce watering in winter while avoiding complete root desiccation.
aspect: Partial shade to full shade. Particularly suitable beneath deciduous trees and along sheltered, shaded borders.
soil: Cool, humus-rich, moisture-retentive soil with adequate drainage. Tolerates acidic, neutral and alkaline conditions.
soilWarning: Avoid hot, dry positions and prolonged winter waterlogging. Rich organic matter improves moisture retention without compromising drainage.
prune: Remove faded flower spikes after flowering and clear damaged or dead foliage in late winter. Divide congested clumps in spring if required.
toxicity: No significant toxicity commonly reported. Not intended for consumption.
compliance: Protected cultivar (PBR); check propagation rights before commercial multiplication.
hardinessNote: Exceptionally cold-hardy when established. Dies back seasonally and returns in spring. Protect roots from excessive winter wet.
resilience: Excellent frost tolerance and shade adaptation. Generally resistant to serious pests, although slugs may damage young foliage and mildew can occur under drought stress.
uses: Woodland gardens, shady ground cover, front-of-border planting, path edging, underplanting trees and naturalistic cottage gardens.

visual: A low-growing, spreading succulent with slender, trailing stems and narrow, fleshy, pale green leaves attractively edged in creamy white. The foliage forms a bright, textured mat, sometimes developing pinkish tones in strong light. Small, star-shaped yellow flowers appear during summer.
water: Allow the compost to dry significantly between waterings. Water moderately during active growth and sparingly in winter. Established plants tolerate periods of drought.
aspect: Full sun is preferred for compact growth and strong variegation. Tolerates light partial shade but may become elongated in insufficient light.
soil: Light, gritty, sharply draining sandy or loamy soil, preferably neutral to alkaline.
soilWarning: Highly vulnerable to persistent wet conditions around the roots, especially during cold weather. Avoid heavy, poorly drained soil and exposed winter-wet positions.
prune: Trim or pinch back elongated stems after flowering to retain compact growth. Remove damaged material and any vigorous plain-green reverted shoots.
toxicity: No major toxicity commonly reported for this cultivar. Avoid ingestion and keep unidentified plant material away from pets.
hardinessNote: Hardy through much of the UK in sheltered, sharply drained positions. Winter wet can be more damaging than cold. Container specimens benefit from rain protection during severe weather.
resilience: Strong drought tolerance, low nutrient requirements and generally good resistance to pests. Susceptible to crown and root rot in persistently wet conditions.
uses: Rock gardens, alpine troughs, sunny containers, hanging baskets, gravel gardens, edging and cascading over low walls.

visual: A delicate trailing succulent houseplant producing long, slender purple-pink stems decorated with small, heart-shaped leaves. Each leaf displays intricate silver-green marbling with creamy white margins, frequently flushed with soft pink in bright light. Unusual narrow, lantern-shaped pink-purple flowers may appear during active growth.
water: Water thoroughly when the majority of the compost has dried, allowing excess water to drain completely. Reduce watering considerably during winter. The tuberous roots store moisture and tolerate short dry periods.
aspect: Bright indirect light with some gentle morning or late afternoon sunshine. Protect from intense midday sunlight behind glass.
soil: Very free-draining cactus or succulent compost with added perlite, pumice or coarse mineral grit.
soilWarning: Avoid continuously damp compost, waterlogged saucers and cold draughts. Insufficient light causes long gaps between leaves and reduced variegation.
prune: Trim excessively long or sparse trailing stems during spring or summer to encourage branching. Propagate healthy stem cuttings or aerial tubers.
toxicity: Generally regarded as non-toxic to cats and dogs, although ingestion may still cause mild gastrointestinal upset.
compliance: Tender houseplant; unsuitable for permanent outdoor cultivation in the UK.
hardinessNote: Frost-tender. Grow indoors throughout the UK winter, preferably maintaining temperatures above 12-15°C. May be placed outdoors during reliably warm summer weather.
resilience: Good drought tolerance and adaptable to typical indoor humidity. Vulnerable to overwatering, cold conditions, mealybugs and occasional scale insects.
uses: Hanging baskets, indoor shelves, trailing houseplant displays, bright windowsills and decorative indoor containers.
uncertain: Ceropegia woodii 'Variegata' is also treated botanically as Ceropegia linearis subsp. woodii 'Variegata'.
Flowering season indoors depends on light and growing conditions.
